chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'The people of Makkah are denying you, saying that you slaughtered your offering in your house in Makkah.' So he said, 'Verily, all of Makkah is a place of sacrifice.'
ai.seo_question: Where can one slaughter their Hajj offering (hady) according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the ruling for the sacrificial offering (hady) during Hajj, stating that the entire area of Makkah is considered a valid place for slaughter, countering those who restricted it to a specific location. This hadith establishes the principle of *Tawassu'* (expansion) in the sanctity of Makkah, distinguishing the permissibility of slaughter from the stricter restrictions on Ihram rituals, thereby facilitating the practice for pilgrims.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The people of Makkah are denying upon you<sup>asws</sup> that you<sup>asws</sup> slaughtered your<sup>asws</sup> offering in your<sup>asws</sup> house in Makkah’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Verily Makkah, the whole of it, is a place for sacrifice’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, that people of Makkah disliked my slaughtering the offering in my lodging in Makkah.
He (the Imam) said, ‘All of Makkah is the place to slaughter offerings.’”
